Galician

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /inˈsɛkto/ [inˈs̺ɛk.t̪ʊ]
  • Rhymes: -ɛkto
  • Hyphenation: in‧sec‧to

Noun

[edit]

insecto m (plural insectos)

  1. insect

Latin

[edit]

Participle

[edit]

īnsectō

  1. dative/ablative masculine/neuter singular of īnsectus

References

[edit]
  • “insecto”, in Charlton T. Lewis and Charles Short (1879), A Latin Dictionary, Oxford: Clarendon Press
  • "insecto", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)
  • “insecto”, in Gaffiot, Félix (1934), Dictionnaire illustré latin-français, Hachette.
  • insecto in Ramminger, Johann (16 July 2016 (last accessed)), Neulateinische Wortliste: Ein Wörterbuch des Lateinischen von Petrarca bis 1700‎[1], pre-publication website, 2005-2016

Portuguese

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

insecto m (plural insectos)

  1. pre-reform spelling (used until 1943 in Brazil and 1990 in Portugal) of inseto; still used where the agreement hasn’t come into effect and may occur as a sporadic misspelling

Further reading

[edit]
  • “insecto”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Romanian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [inˈsekto]

Noun

[edit]

insecto f

  1. vocative singular of insectă

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin īnsecta (“insects”) (attested in Pliny only in the plural), a calque of ἔντομα (éntoma, “insects”, literally “dissected”), from their segmented bodies, from εν- (en-) + τόμος (tómos, “slice”); calqued based on īnsectus (“notched, dissected”), perfect passive participle of īnsecō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /inˈseɡto/ [ĩnˈseɣ̞.t̪o]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -eɡto
  • Syllabification: in‧sec‧to

Noun

[edit]

insecto m (plural insectos)

  1. insect

Derived terms

[edit]
  • insectario
  • insecto hoja
  • insecto palo

Related terms

[edit]
  • insecticida

See also

[edit]
  • bicho

Further reading

[edit]
